rows: Nickel to quarter size hail was reported by the public in Verhalen.
Penny size hail fell on Texas Highway 17 south of Pecos.
Nickel hail covered the ground in Toyah.
Penny to nickel size hail fell in Pecos along both Interstate 20 and U.S. Highway 285.
Nickel size hail fell in a swath along Texas Highway 17 from the Jeff Davis/Reeves County line to Toyahvale.
A trained spotter estimated winds of 64 mph. Trees and power lines were downed by strong winds.
Strong thunderstorm winds downed powerlines north of Pecos.
Pecos Automated Weather Observing System reported a 50 knot gust. No damage was reported.
The duration of the hail was estimated for this event.
Several power poles were knocked down/snapped by the wind gust. The time of this report was estimated according to radar data.

The Reeves County Emergency Manager reported that an old trailer was blown over at approximately 7 PM CST in the city of Pecos, TX. A girl was injured when the trailer fell on top of her.
An estimated 20 to 30 power poles were knocked down or damaged along SH 17.
A severe thunderstorm produced tennis ball sized hail seven miles north of Orla. Winds between 50 and 60 mph occured on State Road 25.
A thunderstorm moved over Orla and produced winds over 60 mph which resulted in broken poles.
A thunderstorm moved over Reeves County and produced one inch hail in Balmorhea. The hail was reported to be an inch deep, and it lasted for ten minutes.
A thunderstorm moved over Reeves County and produced a 71 mph wind gust two miles southwest of Pecos.
A thunderstorm moved over Reeves County and produced a 71 mph wind gust two miles southwest of Pecos.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced an estimated 80 mph wind gust five miles south of Pecos. No damage was reported.

A thunderstorm moved over Reeves County and produced strong winds in Pecos. A roof was blown off of an appliance store, and the gusts were estimated to be near 80 mph. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced wind damage in Balmorhea. There were reports of damage to trees and sheds as well as power outages. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 60 mph wind gust in Pecos. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 59 mph wind gust as measured by the ASOS near Pecos. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced winds around 60 mph. Tree limbs were blown down as a result of these winds. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 59 mph wind gust near Pecos at the ASOS site. No damage was reported.

A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced wind damage in Balmorhea. There was a large tree down at El Paso Street and State Highway 17. The tree was blocking Highway 17. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced golf ball sized hail 4 miles north of the US 285/302 intersection along US 285.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced nickel sized hail along Highway 285.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced two inch hail southwest of Pecos. The hail was covering the ground.

A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced one inch hail southeast of Pecos. The hail was reported to be up to one foot deep covering US 285 with near zero visibility.

A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a tornado south of Pecos. The tornado was seen by a trained spotter 11 miles south of Pecos between Highway 285 and Farm to Market Road 1450. It was on the ground for approximately 5 minutes and no damage was reported. The pa…
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced nickel sized hail east of Balmorhea between mile markers 212 and 214 on Interstate 10.

A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced wind damage in Pecos and Barstow. A tree was knocked down in Pecos and there was tree damage reported in Barstow. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 58 mph wind gust as recorded by the AWOS near the City of Pecos.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 58 mph wind gust at the Pecos Municipal Airport.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced hail damage in Pecos. There were windows broken on about 15 homes. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced wind damage in Pecos. There were powerlines down and damaged trees reported. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 68 mph wind gust two miles south of Pecos.
Golf ball size hail covering I-10 at mile marker 221.
Quarter size hail was covering 25 percent of the road and melting, but passable. Hail was roughly 2 inches deep in a few locations.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 59 mph wind gust eleven miles southeast of Orla.
A thunderstorm moved through Pecos and produced a 64 mph wind gust at the Pecos Airport AWOS.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 64 mph wind gust in Pecos. There were power outages reported in Pecos. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 60 mph wind gust and pea sized hail in Orla.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 62 mph wind gust four miles southwest of Pecos.

A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced damage near Pecos. Roof and structural damage was reported approximately one half mile west of the Pecos Airport. The time was estimated from radar and the wind speed was estimated. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate…
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 59 mph wind gust in Pecos.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced wind damage in the town of Pecos. Power lines were down at 8th Street and Peach Street. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 58 mph wind gust two miles southwest of the town of Pecos.

A thunderstorm in Reeves County produced a tornado about eight miles west of Mentone. A National Weather Service survey team was unable to locate damage directly caused by the tornado due to poor road networks. Photos provided by the public and emergency management suggested that…
A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced a 61 mph wind gust at the Pecos AWOS site.

A thunderstorm moved across Reeves County and produced wind damage near Pecos. It was likely a microburst with winds estimated to be 90 mph. The winds damaged three travel trailers. The time was estimated from radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Landspout: A photo of an apparent landspout tornado near Saragosa was shared on social media. Location and time were estimated by radar. Path length and width were estimated. There was no reported damage with this landspout.
Hail damaged a vehicle's windshield on US Highway 285.
Ping pong ball-sized hail was observed along I-10 near Balmorhea.
Two-inch diameter hail was observed on the south side of Balmorhea.
Lots of small hail, some of the hail may be slightly larger.
A spotter reported dime to quarter size hail.
A storm chaser reported quarter size hail along FM 1450. Time is estimated from radar.
Pecos County Fire Department reported quarter size hail. Time is estimated from radar.
A report of penny size hail was received from MPING. Time is estimated from radar.
Broadcast media shared a report of golf ball sized hail in Pecos. Time is estimated from radar.
Multiple reports of hail the size of golf balls to hen eggs in Pecos. Time verified by reports and radar.
Storm chaser reported hail up to the size of golf balls.
Ping Pong to Golf Ball-size hail reported by the public via social media. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar.
Hen Egg-size hail partially shattering the windshield of a vehicle. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damages is also estimated.
The Mesonet station UR144 14.1 SW Toyah measured a 74 mph wind gust, as well as a 60 mph wind gust. The total duration/time of occurrence is partially estimated.
The Mesonet station TWB47 13.9 SE Toyah Lake measured a 63 mph wind gust. The total duration/time of occurrence is estimated.
